warm_memory.goal: Implement the strongest-brain AI Context Registry and policy-based RBAC rebuild from the reviewed plan.
warm_memory.classification: coding.architecture; backend context-pack pipeline, policy authorization, frontend admin UI, documentation
constraints: Treat AI context as system design/process/function facts for demand deconstruction, not a targeted module feature.
Keep old AI config text fields as backend fallback only so existing deployments do not lose context.
Do not touch or stage unrelated dirty files such as `well-ambient.db` or `internal/server/task_status.md`.
decisions: Added Context Registry models for documents, facts, chunks, packs, and pack items.
Demand deconstruction now builds and persists a context pack before prompt assembly, returns `context_pack_id`, and archives that pack id during import.
AI settings now exposes structured context facts and pack preview while removing the old visible four-textarea context center; legacy config fields remain fallback only.
Added policy authorization tables and evaluator with explicit deny override, policy allow grants, super_admin break-glass, legacy group permission compatibility, and decision audit logging.
Added policy management and authorization explanation UI under Settings.
findings: Structured facts give demand deconstruction a compact, auditable context layer with scope, freshness, confidence, token count, and hash metadata.
Persisted context packs make estimate archives reproducible because the system can inspect which context facts were used for a run.
Policy RBAC can evolve without breaking existing users by placing allow/deny policies above the current group-permission matrix.
Full Go tests need loopback access because existing GitLab webhook tests use `httptest.NewServer`; sandboxed runs fail on local port binding.
validation: GOCACHE=/tmp/well-ambient-gocache go test ./...: passed with approved loopback access after sandbox port bind failed.
